newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas selling.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas selling.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold market slid on professional selling from the United States and Europe, but most players were focused on a jittery silver market, gold dealers in the British territory said on Friday.
"There was some selling interest from the U.S. and Europe, probably on disappointment at gold's performance," said one source at an international bank's local office.
Buyers were scarce in the loco London market, traders said.
But gold was also simply following silver's downtrend, sources said.
"There is very strong support for silver at $4.90," one gold trader said.
The shortage of kilobars in Hong Kong will likely be eased next week, pushing premiums down slightly, traders said.
Bullion ended at US$382.30/382.80 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$382.50/383.00 close on Thursday.
Local gold ended HK$7 lower at HK$3,525 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at -5.
